meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, Hale?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

Forty minutes in a classroom with no book against a weekend at home with the play open in front of him. Of course one has quotations and the other doesn't. And you still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Then show me the version history, because so far I've heard about it and seen nothing. And a classroom sample written without the book tells me nothing about the essay.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me, and confirmation that nothing about this is on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed, she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing placed on his record; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached, because the meeting ended before her time ran out.
What moved her: Nothing; your comparison with the September 24 in-class writing was specific and dated, but she had an easy answer for it and you never met that answer with something she could check.
What cost ground: You never said who decided on the zero or why nobody called her first, and that procedural gap is the ground she fights on hardest.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never got near that night, since you named the version history but showed no times from it; that moment proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided, own entering the zero before calling home in one sentence, then put the version history on the screen with its dates and times instead of only naming it.
